text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text. This training data includes books, websites, and articles, which helps the model learn grammar, facts, and ideas. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like answering questions, summarizing texts, and writing drafts. However, they also have limits: they can make mistakes, sometimes produce false information, and do not truly understand meaning like humans do.
